## Making the firmware
I tried to use the firmware that was recommended by the hackpad's guide, but I tried checking the qmk chip compatibility, and i couldn't find an option for a seeduino moudle xiao (the controller im planning on using), so I instead used ZMK.
(Didn't count this time cuz i was learning but i prolly spent like 2 hours just trying to figure out how to use the zmk cli and github cli nonsense (i think i recorded myself doing that. think you might need to cut that time. i dunno if it counts as learning or trying and failing)). In the end i cloned [the firmware config thing](https://github.com/zmkfirmware/unified-zmk-config-template) and edited+githubbed it in vscode
First 30 mins of coding, crunched out hackpadd.overlay
![VsCode image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/W1c28oFzhqawCAaFFBFieXuylI2NJFjr/8e7eb6da7dcd8c2b3b30ac45b31b1739c9cc5a2141adf3caa2b7982448ac464a.png)

Then 40 minutes coding and thinking of key layout for hackpadd.keymap. I can up with 3 layers of commands.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/W1c28oFzhqawCAaFFBFieXuylI2NJFjr/c4aa3080c8902f25cd8281c46d433fb9b894a1f891e504426ebfd3adad7abb92.png)
(the general gist is layer one is alt tab, show desktop, task manager, music controls, cut copy paste, undo redo, and a key to access layer two. Layer two is just function keys 13-21 and a key to acces layer 3, for per-application shortcuts (also because my keyboard doesnt have those f keys). Layer 3 is like power off and reset and bootloader. Crazy stuff i hope i never need.

Then spent like 10 minutes doing the rest of the files (it effectively felt like filling out forms (i didnt include time learning *how* to fill out said forms))

## Issues
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/W1c28oFzhqawCAaFFBFieXuylI2NJFjr/0d04f7be26911b21069c66d3418713e3eadc84c63cad289efeaec078cc6082c2.png)
Ruh oh, error. gotta fix it (it was the wrong zmk version. fix: change "revision" to main)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/W1c28oFzhqawCAaFFBFieXuylI2NJFjr/46c9a90b15dde18cd85a9a6f091934245b4cf0fdaaa2d047377e9a0673c5c871.png)
It took 12 fixes (including the first one) :(
I'm not going to list every error+fix, cause most of them were just typos, but some standouts are:
1: it needed a physical layout, fix: i added a default layout based on the guide
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/W1c28oFzhqawCAaFFBFieXuylI2NJFjr/8eb758cb991a8f2fb829c386fff9078bf56214ef2b6ca5a762ff0c1501679a08.png)
2: I put a node (i dunno how to explain it. its like a property of the macropad? in this case it was the node was connecting the default physical layout to the electrical wired keyboard matrix) in the wrong spot
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/W1c28oFzhqawCAaFFBFieXuylI2NJFjr/29583bcfffcaa5e94c460b7c2f6d21c5159e53d34cae587e61d4f59bfa5d6cea.png)
In the image you see how &layoutless is below and outside of a bracket (};)?, the error was that i put &layoutless inside of the bracket

3: this is just a typo but the typo was in the compatible = "whatever bro just look at the image", and instead of doing matrix-transformation, i used a _, and because compatible defines what that node means, the error didnt say: there's a typo, it said: keymap not found, and it said it in computer language, so i had to noogle around and ask claude what the error message meant, and it took more time than the typical typo
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/W1c28oFzhqawCAaFFBFieXuylI2NJFjr/98d8056085762f4c424cbf62d7453a644458e560e37c39e070964c2aad5c901e.png)

and finally, 4: part of the firmware creating process requires something called artifact renaming or smth, because i didnt name the artifact. So i added an artifact name
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/W1c28oFzhqawCAaFFBFieXuylI2NJFjr/5da577a0d61b86aecda871a08cebc375e95098a4487bd574b35b522390cd1b80.png)
